_help.sea_cave_boom: Design §DX (the columns, added by Claude Code, 4 Oct): the swell striking the back of the columned sea cave, once a swell (Landmarks SWELL_S, 7-11 s; SoundSynth boom). A source at the cave's back: played only while you are within max_distance, so you hear it from the clifftop before you have found the way down; muffled with distance like any source.
_help.bench_kinds: Design 5 Oct §EL (the workshop, added by Claude Code): scrape, cord_twist, needle_through_hide (the soft bench) and tap_tap, grind, drill_whirr (the hard bench) are the benches' work sounds (camps.json sim.workshop.benches[].sounds; Workshop, SoundSynth <kind>_loop): short quiet loops from the bench itself while a folk works at it, each idle its own (sew_with_awl the needle, twist_cord and plait_basket the cord, scrape_hide the scrape; knap the tap-tap, grind_axe and hollow_bowl_with_coal the grind, bow_drill the whirr). A source like any other (§BG): heard from the door, gone at max_distance.
_help.crown_kinds: Design §DA (Wind II, added by Claude Code, 4 Oct): crown_hush, crown_rustle, crown_clatter, crown_rattle are the crowns round you sounding in the gusts (WindCrowns; wind.json sound.crowns): a source at each crown, voiced by its leaf (needles hush, broad leaves rustle, palm fronds clatter, dry autumn leaves rattle; SoundSynth crown_*_loop), muffled like any source so you can walk to it.
_help.strike_tell: Design 6 Oct §FA.2 (prompt 57, added by Claude Code): a creature's strike tell, its own sound as it winds up to strike (CreatureStrike; the creature's strike.sound names the SoundSynth voice, the snake's snake_hiss). A source at the creature's head from the wind-up's first frame: loud close by, so an ambush is heard before it is seen; dull and without direction far off, like any source.
_help.kinds: One row per kind of world sound; every 3D sound player in the game takes its row (Audio3D.apply).
_help.boss_kinds: Design §EY (the dungeon's boss, added by Claude Code, 7 Oct, queue 49; Boss, BossSounds): boss_tell is its tell and its hiss (the snake: scales dragging on stone, heard through the tomb well before it is seen, max_distance 34 against the torch's few metres of sight); boss_breath its breathing in its hole once it has been driven home (max_distance is overridden by bosses.json lair.breathing_heard_m); boss_cry the release, the long sound going away along the tomb and down into the hole.
_help.unit_size: Meters within which the sound plays at full loudness; past it, it fades with distance.
_help.max_distance: Meters past which it is not heard at all; it also fades out linearly toward this distance, so it never cuts off.
_help.model: How it fades past unit_size: inverse (about 6 dB quieter each time the distance doubles, like real sound in the open), inverse_square (12 dB, for small sounds that should die fast), log (steeper still), none (no fading, only max_distance).
_help.max_db: Loudest boost (dB) when you are closer than unit_size (0: never louder than set).
_help.muffle: [near m, far m] or null: from near to far the sound loses its high end (down to muffle_far.cutoff_hz) and most of its direction (panning down to muffle_far.pan), as a far howl does. null: always clear.
_help.muffle_far: Where a muffled sound ends up at its far distance: cutoff_hz (its brightest frequency) and pan (0-1, how much of its left-right direction is left).
_help.cloak_flurry: Design §Z: the whip-and-rustle of heavy cloth on every roll, slide start, wall-jump kick and swing release (synthesized in sound_synth, no sample). pitch_by_speed: how much faster movement sharpens the snap (0 = same every time). noise_m: how far creatures hear it. volume_db: loudness.
_help.class: Design 30 Sept §BG: every kind is a SOURCE (a 3D player at a place you can walk to; muffle: the far and near distances between which terrain and foliage dull it) or lives in the BED below (no position). Both lists together file every sound in the game.
_help.fire_block: Design 30 Sept night §BZ (pushed 1 Oct): two layers at every fire, both SOURCES (kinds.fire): hiss, a steady soft bed (volume_db, cutoff_hz), and pops — snaps and crackles as ONE-SHOTS on a random clock (every_s between pops, a loudness band, a pitch band, snaps_share the sharp ones), never the 4 s fire_loop cycle the ear learns. low_fire: fewer, quieter pops as the store burns down; embers only hiss. hear_before_seen: kinds.fire.max_distance raised so on the first road you hear the camp before you see its glow. First guesses; the designer owns them.

_help_bed: Design 30 Sept §BG: sounds are either the ambient BED ("bed" below, SoundBed: no position; wind, insects, distant birds, frogs; per biome group, hour and season; it thins at dread stage 1) or a point SOURCE (every row in "kinds": a 3D player at a place you can walk to, muffled by terrain and foliage where muffle is set). Filed 30 Sept: bed = wind, insects, birds_far, frogs. Sources = every kinds row: the player's own (footstep, player_voice, bow, arrow, spear, spear_impact, climb_hand, climb_breath, torch, torch_light), the world's (rustle: the litter and the trees you brush; rain: the rain FX round the camera; fire: every campfire's crackle; water_flow and waterfall: the rivers and their falls; camp_chatter; thunder; meteor), the creatures' (wildlife_call: one animal calling from where it is; howl; gibbon_hoot; rider_hooves; crawler_hands; mythic_call; hoofbeats_far) and the dark's (dread_follow, dread_close). The HUD's hit tick is UI, neither.

bed._help: The ambient bed (SoundBed): four loops with no position (wind, insects, distant birds, frogs), mixed by biome group x hour x season x weather; frogs only near water (frogs_near_water_km); insects and frogs silent below cold_c_silence C; the wind loop by the wind's own speed (gain_per_mps) and closed under canopy (canopy: gain and low-pass cutoff by how much sky the place sees). Levels are linear gains 0-1; layers.db trims each loop. It thins at dread stage 1 (Dread.bed_gain). Added by Claude Code as a feel call on 30 Sept (the designer owns it from here).

ruins._help: A ruin sounds like what lives in it (Mike, 3 Oct by voice: "we need to have some ambient sounds based off of what type of creatures are lurking there"), inside §BG's two systems. residents are SOURCES, each calling from the part of the ruin it lives in, at its hours (the creature itself comes from the biome's roster, §CH; these name the place and the kind). The swifts in a cold stack are §CV.5 (smoke.json swifts.sound). bed: the ruin's own room tone, with no position: wind in the stones (gaps, doorways, window holes and cave mouths moan when the gust at them passes stone_wind_from_mps, wind.json), drips where there is water, and the hush of a closed hall. overrun: an overrun ruin's residents fall silent by day (delves.json overrun tells). The ghost (ruins.json haunt) makes no sound at all. Not written: Minecraft's cave groans, whose unplaceable noises are what §BG took out on 30 Sept; Mike's call (§DI, open).

residents.kind: nesting birds: the roster's cliff and cavity nesters (jackdaws, rock doves where they live); swifts over a cold stack are §CV.5
bats pouring out and streaming back (§CH)
something small scrabbling in the dark: the night roster's small ground animals
lizards rustling in the dry stones (warm country)
